clue.text: Fruity thing — could have you on your back in no time

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the peel of a yellow tropical fruit

definitions.text: could have you on your back in no time
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a slippery hazard, or figuratively a blunder that floors you

explanation.walkthrough: The surface hints at a fast seduction; the real picture is the comedy pratfall on discarded fruit peel.
explanation.definitionFit: Stepping on yellow peel is the classic slapstick cause of a sudden fall, and figuratively a blunder.

clue.text: Bye bye Jewish prick when church ousted by ring

indicators.note: ousted by means one piece is pushed out and replaced by the other

parts.note: schlong is Yiddish slang for a penis
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A farewell joke about circumcision, the church losing out to the ring.
explanation.definitionFit: So long is an informal farewell meaning goodbye.

clue.text: Shagged to death on society engagements such as these?

definitions.meaning: the sexual outcome hoped for from a romantic meeting
points at a type of social appointment where passion runs high

explanation.walkthrough: The clue describes the result, exhausting sex, and asks what kind of engagement would lead to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot date is an exciting romantic outing expected to end in passion.

clue.text: Cover boob by arse-over-tip official

parts.note: tit is slang for a breast

indicators.note: arse-over-tip means head over heels, upside down, so this word is reversed in a down entry

parts.note: a ref is a referee, a match official

explanation.surface: A boob is covered up by an official who falls head over heels.
explanation.walkthrough: Titfer is Cockney rhyming slang for a hat, from tit for tat.
explanation.definitionFit: A titfer is a hat, a head covering.

clue.text: Wait a minute, Tony's pissed about Conservative's last poster

indicators.note: about means the jumbled name goes around the other letters
pissed means drunk, so the letters reel into a new order

parts.note: the name with its s

indicators.note: last picks the final letter of the word

parts.note: an ad, short for advertisement, is a poster

explanation.surface: A cry of caution as Tony Blair, drunk, wrecks a Tory campaign billboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Steady on is a British exclamation urging someone to calm down or not go too far.

clue.text: Branson's thing: kicking arse for Lake poet

indicators.note: the arse is the tail end, so the last letter is kicked out and the other letter takes its place

parts.note: Richard Branson founded the Virgin brand
L is a map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Richard Branson's company gets tough in favour of one of the Lake District poets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lake poet' looks like Wordsworth or Coleridge, but Lake only supplies a letter and the poet is Roman.
explanation.definitionFit: Virgil was the Roman author of the Aeneid, a classical epic poet.

clue.text: Sun: "Big One On Stud!"

parts.note: S is the calendar abbreviation for Sunday
tall means big in height
I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Sun tabloid headline boasting about a well-endowed man.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid; here it is just the abbreviation of Sunday.
explanation.definitionFit: A stallion is a male horse kept for breeding, which is exactly what a stud animal is.

clue.text: Piss-artist in the Lords?

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read literally and jokily: one who pees
second meaning: a member of the House of Lords

explanation.walkthrough: Piss-artist is British slang for a drunk, but here it is taken literally as someone who pees; the question mark flags the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer is a noble with a seat in the House of Lords, and a pee-er is one who urinates.

clue.text: One onto Charlie's game: "Stupid git's a defender of the faith?"

indicators.note: onto says the first piece is followed straight away by what comes next

parts.note: one is A, the indefinite article
Prince Charles was famous for playing polo

indicators.note: stupid suggests the letters of git's are muddled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A sneer at a dim polo-playing prince who bears the royal title Defender of the Faith.
explanation.walkthrough: Defender of the Faith is a title of the British monarch, which Charles was heir to; the answer is a general word for anyone who argues a case for a belief.
explanation.definitionFit: An apologist argues in support of a doctrine or cause, typically a religious one.

clue.text: Saucy Eye feature: 'Ten nameless men Horatio screwed'

indicators.note: screwed means messed up, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: N is the abbreviation for name, so nameless means men loses its N

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A smutty magazine item about ten anonymous men and someone called Horatio having sex.
explanation.walkthrough: Eye is Private Eye, the British satirical magazine; the Commons tearoom is where MPs gossip, so a column overheard there is a natural Eye feature.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a gossip section set among MPs in their Westminster refreshment room, a likely source of indiscreet stories.

clue.text: Some of Wimbledon's stock bullshit?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a large quantity of the tennis equipment kept for the Wimbledon championships
second meaning: the British slang phrase for nonsense

explanation.walkthrough: Wimbledon is the London tennis tournament, which gets through thousands of balls; 'a load of balls' is British slang for rubbish talk.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is literally a heap of tennis balls and idiomatically a dismissal of something as nonsense.

clue.text: Like Kate Moss: no good in Laura's new creation

indicators.note: in means the other letters go inside
a new creation is something remade, so the name's letters are rearranged

parts.note: Laura, the possessive marking that the rearrangement is hers

explanation.surface: A fashion designer Laura's new collection made for model Kate Moss.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's only ties the creation to Laura; her name alone is rearranged, with the no-good letters set inside after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Kate Moss is a famously thin model, so bony and lean, which is angular.

clue.text: Bangs Ted, loses plot, resulting in unsettling feeling

indicators.note: loses tells us the letters for plot are taken out of the two names

parts.note: a bed is a garden plot, as in a flower bed

explanation.surface: Bangs, Ted, loses the plot: a Private Eye jibe at someone going wild and ending up anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses plot' reads as going mad, but the plot is a garden bed, and its letters are split across both names: one off the front of the first, two off the end of the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Angst is a German loanword for a deep feeling of dread or anxiety.

clue.text: Money-maker Brenda's bloomer?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the body that manufactures British coins
second meaning: a herb belonging to the Queen, Brenda being Private Eye's nickname for her

explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye calls the Queen Brenda; a bloomer is a flowering plant here, not a mistake, and mint is a herb.
explanation.definitionFit: The Royal Mint is the UK's coin manufacturer, and read whimsically it is a mint herb belonging to royalty.

clue.text: Gathering of politicians: tense males, undistinguished on the inside

indicators.note: on the inside says the undistinguished word sits within the other letters

parts.note: he is a male, so males are hes
common means ordinary, lacking distinction

explanation.surface: A complaint that a political assembly is full of nervous, mediocre men.
explanation.walkthrough: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense.
explanation.definitionFit: The House of Commons is the elected chamber of the UK Parliament, an assembly of MPs.

clue.text: Party that makes you puke three different ways!

indicators.note: different suggests the letters are made into something else by rearranging

parts.note: taken as written
three ways, that is three compass points: north, east and south

explanation.surface: A party so boozy that guests are sick in every direction.
explanation.walkthrough: The ways are points of the compass, N, E and S, which join the four letters of puke for the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A knees-up is British slang for a lively, noisy celebration with dancing and drinking.

clue.text: Guts involves embracing Right

indicators.note: embracing means holding something inside, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: entails means involves or requires

explanation.surface: A political remark that having guts means taking in right-wing views.
explanation.definitionFit: Entrails are a creature's intestines, its innards.

clue.text: One lot misrepresented and framed by tabloid images, but it's what MPs are all about

indicators.note: framed by puts the scrambled letters inside the image word, as a picture sits in its frame

parts.note: pics is tabloid slang for photographs

indicators.note: misrepresented says these letters are presented in a false order

parts.note: One gives I, the Roman numeral, and lot is taken as written

explanation.surface: Tabloid photographs misrepresent a group of people, which is what Members of Parliament really care about.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of Parliament exist to debate, legislate and govern, so the business of government is their whole concern.

clue.text: Sort of theatre pit associated with France's extreme right wing candidate

parts.note: No, also spelt Noh, is classical Japanese drama
a pit is a mine, as in coal pit

indicators.note: the extreme right end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Talk of the French far right's presidential hopeful and theatre seating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'France's extreme right wing' points at the Le Pen far right, but it just takes the last letter of France.
explanation.definitionFit: A nominee is a person put forward for election or office.

clue.text: Peter familiarly 'gobbling' in the manner of the eastern city

indicators.note: gobbling means swallowing, so the name takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: Mandy is the familiar nickname of the politician Peter Mandelson
a la is French for in the style of

explanation.surface: A sly sexual innuendo about a well-known Peter behaving like someone from an Eastern city.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Mandelson, a Labour politician, was widely nicknamed Mandy.
explanation.definitionFit: Mandalay is a large city in Myanmar, formerly Burma, in Asia.

clue.text: Testicle removed — a hindrance appreciated by the vegetarian?

parts.note: nut is slang for a testicle
cut means removed, as in a castration
a let is an obstacle, as in 'without let or hindrance'

explanation.surface: A castration and its awkwardness, oddly welcomed by a meat-avoider.
explanation.walkthrough: The defining phrase is loose: it describes the dish as one a meat-free eater enjoys.
explanation.definitionFit: A nut cutlet is a patty made from chopped nuts, a classic meatless main course.

clue.text: Peacekeepers quite ugly

parts.note: UN peacekeepers are the United Nations' troops
just can mean quite or exactly, as in 'just so'

explanation.surface: A blunt remark that blue-helmeted soldiers are rather unattractive.
explanation.definitionFit: Ugly can mean morally offensive or unfair, as in an ugly decision, close to unfair treatment.

clue.text: Members' exaggerated representations — most crap — about Lawrence

indicators.note: about says the jumbled letters go round the initials
crap means bad or broken, so the letters of most are muddled

parts.note: taken as written
T. E. Lawrence, Lawrence of Arabia

explanation.surface: Mocking phallic carvings as overstated and rubbish, with a nod to D. H. or T. E. Lawrence.
explanation.walkthrough: Members here are penises; a carved pole is pictured as an outsized one.
explanation.definitionFit: Totems are carved emblematic figures, and totem poles are jokingly read as phallic symbols.

clue.text: King George into 'new black'

indicators.note: into says the royal letters are put inside the other word

parts.note: neo is a prefix meaning new
GR is George Rex, the royal cipher of King George

explanation.surface: A fashion slogan claiming a king has become the new black.
explanation.walkthrough: Negro is the Spanish and Portuguese word for black, and also a dated term for a Black person.
explanation.definitionFit: In Spanish the word simply means the colour, the darkest shade.

clue.text: Bang? Lola snapped, — hasn't got an earthly!"

indicators.note: snapped means broken, so the remaining letters are rearranged
hasn't got means the letters an are missing from the words

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Lola tells someone hoping for sex that they have no chance at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hasn't got an earthly' is the British idiom for having no chance; here 'an' is lost from the fodder and 'earthly' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Global means relating to the whole world, the Earth as a whole.

clue.text: Earl's broadcast stream of piss, possibly used by high-flying executives

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered, so the letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: the word Earl; the possessive ending is ignored
a jet is a forceful stream of liquid

explanation.surface: A crude picture of an aristocrat urinating, then a nod to business jets.
explanation.definitionFit: A Learjet is a make of small private business aircraft favoured by wealthy bosses.

clue.text: Grease is needed to make Lulu better!

indicators.note: the answer is needed to make up the run of letters across the two words, sitting inside them

parts.note: the letters are found spanning the end of Lulu and the start of better

explanation.surface: A cheeky suggestion that the singer Lulu would perform better with some lubricant.
explanation.walkthrough: Lulu is a Scottish pop singer; the exclamation mark flags the innuendo.
explanation.definitionFit: Lube is informal for a lubricant, an oil or grease that reduces friction.

clue.text: See 10
See 11
What did you say? Have another orgasm?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a request to repeat something not heard
second meaning: an invitation to climax once more

explanation.walkthrough: One phrase is a polite request for repetition and, read literally, a bawdy offer.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an informal way to ask someone to repeat a remark, and in slang 'come' means climax.
